title: A duplicate table read points to the existing table
runtime: Offline only; no Docker, database, API listener or deployment.

report.WORKS: A completed-table 409 in the standalone import dialog offers Open that table, using the existing source-backed table page.
report.INPUTS: mi-d10-02.csv; mi-d19-01.xlsx, RBI T_18 with header rows 4 and 5; existing generated test_only controls.
report.GAPS: Live browser/navigation, keyboard traversal and zoom remain unqualified; no runtime used.

refusals.message: This original is already a table; open its table page.
refusals.details: existingTable: { caseId, sourceId, tableId }; this application's table ID is its source ID

refusals.message: This original is already being read as a table; follow that read.
refusals.details: existingTable: { caseId, sourceId, jobId }; job ID is read from the existing queued/running job

design: originalTableTx adds a table reference only after the existing case and operator checks and only for an actual table receipt. No source/object is copied, reread or written by the refusal.
queueTableProfileTx returns the existing read job in details without queuing another. Server status, codes and messages are unchanged.
TableImportDialog validates the completed table reference in the existing untyped error details and reuses tablePath for a router link. useRetainTable's existing 409 request-key reset is unchanged.
A queued read is not yet a table page: its dialog words remain unchanged. Other errors and malformed or absent details still use TableRefusal.
The common published 409 envelope already permits details. No route or schema changed; only two implementation source pins changed. OpenAPI and generated client output have no content diff.

inputs.result: First read validates as a table; a new request for the same source returns 409 with its table reference. A second object read is forbidden by the test; hash, case revision and job count remain unchanged.
Same duplicate-read assertions pass for the real multi-header RBI workbook; licence remains unconfirmed.

safety.environment: Verification Node processes used NODE_OPTIONS=--require=<preload> to refuse .env, runtime and forbidden split-path filesystem access before application imports. No protected file was opened.
safety.python: ULPIN_PROFILE_PYTHON=E:/BhuAayam-data/ml/venv-k3a-geo/Scripts/python.exe enabled the existing workbook tests. Scratch files stayed in the existing temporary-directory test paths.

server.signature: Completed and queued duplicate-read errors had no details.

studio.signature: The completed-table dialog had no plain words/link. The initial queued-link assertion was later narrowed to preserve unfinished-read words because that table page is not ready.

checks.note: Initial test launches returned 1 because dependencies were absent; offline install downloaded nothing.
The first openapi --check returned 1 for stale implementation pins, not schema drift.
Generated client has no content change.
Scanner covers apps/web; Studio diff also checked directly.

recovery: An initial Studio schema import failed typecheck: that module has a deliberately narrow declaration surface. The dialog instead validates its untyped error-detail IDs locally without widening shared contracts or declarations.

The first full Studio run exposed an existing complete hook mock that did not include a new helper export. Keeping the error-detail reader private to the dialog removed that seam; the final full intake set passes.
